job.title: Return to Work Coordinator
job.description:
About Them
Our client is a leading, ASX-listed restaurant operator with a national footprint and a large, diverse workforce. Based in Hamilton, their Brisbane support office brings together the teams that support restaurant operations across Australia. You’ll join a supportive safety and wellbeing team that takes a practical, people-focused approach to helping injured employees recover and return to work.

The opportunity
Supporting a national portfolio, predominantly across Queensland, you will help coordinate workers’ compensation claims and suitable duties arrangements. Your responsibilities will include:
  • Providing claim forms and guiding team members through the lodgement process.
  • Following up paperwork, answering questions and keeping claims progressing.
  • Developing, updating and monitoring suitable duties plans.
  • Supporting team members and managers throughout the return to work process.
  • Maintaining accurate and confidential records.
Most existing claims already have suitable duties plans in place. You will have guidance and support from your manager, with minimal insurer engagement and no direct doctor or rehabilitation provider liaison expected during this assignment.

About you
You bring experience in return to work or injury management, sound workers’ compensation knowledge and a Queensland Rehabilitation and Return to Work Coordinator qualification.

You are organised, empathetic and comfortable picking up the phone to support people and follow things through. Confidence learning new systems is essential; experience with the business’s specific platform is not required.

Interested?
Apply now or contact Keilee Armstrong at The Safe Step on karmstrong@thesafestep.com.au for a confidential discussion.

job.title: HSEQ Project Manager
job.description:
The Opportunity
An opportunity exists for an experienced HSEQ (Safety and Quality) Project Manager to lead safety, quality and environmental performance across a major greenfield commercial construction project in the Newcastle region.
This is a large, technically complex build with a substantial electrical construction and fit out component and a significant workforce expected on site through peak construction.
Sitting as part of the Project Senior Management Team, this is much more than a traditional site safety role. You will lead HSEQ across the project, providing direction across safety, quality, assurance, contractor management and operational risk from mobilisation through construction, fit out and commissioning.

The Role
Leading a dedicated project Safety and Quality team, your responsibilities will include:
  • Leading HSEQ performance across the project
  • Providing visible leadership across a large construction workforce
  • Leading and developing project safety and quality resources
  • Driving risk management, assurance and governance
  • Partnering with project leaders and contractors to improve WHSEQ performance
  • Providing oversight of quality processes across complex electrical construction and fit out
  • Supporting HSEQ systems, processes and continuous improvement
  • Contributing as a key member of the senior project leadership team
About You
We are looking for an established HSEQ professional with experience across major construction, electrical, engineering or infrastructure projects.
You will ideally bring:
  • Strong project based safety leadership experience
  • Exposure to electrical construction, fit out or complex building services
  • Experience within large greenfield construction environments
  • Genuine Quality and assurance capability
  • Experience leading HSEQ or project safety teams
  • Strong contractor and stakeholder management capability
  • The credibility to influence senior project and operational leaders
Electrical construction experience would be highly regarded, particularly across large commercial builds, complex electrical installations or highly serviced facilities.

job.title: Work Health and Safety Coordinator I AHCSA
job.description:
Aboriginal Health Council of South Australia (AHCSA)

Make a meaningful contribution across South Australia.

About the organisation
As the health voice for Aboriginal people in South Australia, AHCSA advocates for communities and our Member Services, supporting the delivery of culturally appropriate health programs grounded in a holistic understanding of health and wellbeing.
  
“Our Health, Our Choice, Our Way” is at the heart of AHCSA's identity, reflecting its commitment to Aboriginal self-determination, cultural safety and strengthening the Aboriginal community-controlled health sector.  Guided by the principle of Aboriginal health in Aboriginal hands, AHCSA is committed to supporting Aboriginal people and communities to have a voice in decisions affecting their health and wellbeing.
  
About the opportunity
AHCSA is seeking an experienced Work Health and Safety professional to lead and strengthen its approach to workplace health, safety and wellbeing.
  
This is an opportunity to make a genuine difference in an organisation where psychological safety, cultural respect and employee wellbeing are just as important as legislative compliance.
  
Working across the organisation and with Member Services, you will build relationships, develop capability and ensure WHS practices are practical, accessible and responsive to the needs of AHCSA's people.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Lead the development, implementation and continuous improvement of AHCSA's WHS Management System, policies and procedures.
  • Manage WHS governance, risk assessments, audits, incident investigations and regulatory compliance.
  • Identify and manage psychosocial hazards, strengthening psychological safety and workplace wellbeing.
  • Embed cultural safety principles into WHS practices, recognising the importance of cultural identity, lived experience and community.
  • Chair the WHS Committee and provide advice and guidance to senior leaders and employees.
  • Coordinate WHS training, inductions, reporting and Return to Work activities.
  • Build capability and encourage employee engagement in workplace health and safety.
About you
You will bring sound technical WHS knowledge and experience, together with the interpersonal skills, cultural awareness and judgement to work effectively within AHCSA.
  
You are approachable, a good listener and someone who takes the time to build genuine relationships and understand different perspectives. You recognise that creating a safe workplace goes beyond policies and procedures, and that trust, respect and open communication are fundamental to achieving positive outcomes.
  
You will bring:
  • Experience or demonstrated capability in psychosocial risk management, psychological safety and workplace wellbeing.
  • The ability to engage respectfully with Aboriginal and non-Aboriginal employees, leaders and stakeholders.
  • Strong communication and influencing skills, with the confidence to provide advice and constructively challenge when required.
  • A practical, collaborative approach to problem-solving, continuous improvement and building WHS capability.
  
A Diploma of Work Health and Safety, or Certificate IV in Work Health and Safety with substantial demonstrated experience at coordinator level, is essential.
  
Experience within community cantered environment will be highly regarded.
  
Why join AHCSA?
AHCSA offers the opportunity to contribute to an organisation making a meaningful difference to Aboriginal health and wellbeing across South Australia.
  
Along with a supportive, culturally respectful and purpose-driven workplace, benefits include:
  • Generous not-for-profit salary packaging.
  • Two additional weeks of paid leave over the Christmas period.
  • Four weeks of annual leave with 17.5% leave loading.
  • Employee Assistance Program.
  • Flexible working arrangements and professional development support.
  
How to apply
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants are strongly encouraged to apply.

Cultural knowledge, lived experience and community connections are recognised and valued.

Applications are also welcomed from people of all backgrounds who demonstrate the experience, cultural awareness and commitment to AHCSA's values required for this position.
  
To apply, please submit your resume and a covering letter outlining your interest and relevant experience.

job.title: HSEQ Business Partner
job.description:
The Opportunity

Our client is an established and growing essential services business operating across multiple sites, providing critical services to customers across a diverse operational environment.
  
With a busy workforce, multiple operational locations and a combination of transport, plant and site based activities, health and safety is an important part of how the business operates. The organisation is continuing to strengthen its approach to HSEQ, creating an opportunity for a Coordinator or developing Advisor to join the team and play a key role in that journey.
  
This is a broad, hands on position with exposure across operational health and safety, risk, incidents, compliance, audits, systems and improvement projects. There is plenty to do and plenty to learn, making it well suited to someone who wants more responsibility and broader experience. 
  
Importantly, you will work closely with an exceptional leader who is approachable, supportive and genuinely invested in developing people. You will have someone to learn from and bounce ideas off, while being given the autonomy to build confidence and take greater ownership over time.
  
What You'll Do
  • Support day to day health, safety, environment and compliance activities across operational sites
  • Work with operational teams on risk assessments, controls and safety improvements
  • Support incident investigations and ensure actions are followed through
  • Coordinate workplace inspections, audits and compliance activities
  • Support the continued development and implementation of HSEQ systems and processes
  • Work closely with leaders, supervisors and frontline teams to strengthen safety engagement
  • Assist with training, injury management and broader HSEQ initiatives
  • Maintain safety documentation, records and compliance requirements
  • Help work through existing compliance priorities and keep actions moving
  • Contribute to projects and improvement initiatives as the safety function continues to develop  
What You Bring
  • Experience in a health and safety role, ideally within an operational environment
  • A relevant health and safety qualification
  • An approachable, practical style and the confidence to build relationships across the business
  • Strong organisation skills with the ability to work through competing priorities
  • Curiosity and a genuine willingness to learn and develop
  • Initiative and the confidence to take ownership while remaining open to guidance
  • Good judgement and the ability to understand what needs attention first
  • Comfort balancing time in the operation with compliance and administration
  • A genuine interest in people and improving safety outcomes
  • The ability to work through ambiguity without needing every process or answer already mapped out
Experience across waste, transport, logistics, manufacturing, chemicals or another operational environment would be beneficial, but is not essential.
  
Why Consider This Opportunity?
  
There are two real drawcards to this opportunity: the leader and the breadth of the role.
  
You will work with a highly regarded health and safety leader who genuinely enjoys developing people and will give you the support, guidance and exposure to keep building your career.
  
You will also join a health and safety function that is continuing to evolve. Not everything is finished or perfectly established, and that is part of the opportunity. You will be able to get involved in a wide range of work, contribute ideas and build experience across areas you may not currently have exposure to.

job.title: HSE Advisor
job.description:
The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to join a growing renewable energy business with an expanding portfolio of projects and operational assets across Australia.

Working across development, construction and operations, the HSE Advisor will provide practical support and guidance to project teams, operational leaders and contractors across the business.

The role has a strong focus on contractor management, risk and assurance, while also supporting incident management, reporting, HSE systems and broader improvement initiatives. Rather than building from scratch, you will be joining a business with established frameworks and standards that now need to be consistently applied as the organisation and its portfolio continue to grow.

What You’ll Do
  • Partner with project, development and operational teams to provide practical HSE advice and support
  • Strengthen contractor management, oversight and assurance across projects and operational assets
  • Support risk management activities and ensure key HSE risks are understood and effectively managed
  • Participate in incident investigations, reviews and corrective actions, ensuring learnings are carried through the business
  • Coordinate audit and assurance activities and support the close out of identified actions
  • Contribute to HSE performance reporting, including monthly and board reporting
  • Support the consistent application of existing HSE policies, standards and management systems
  • Build the confidence and capability of leaders and teams to take greater ownership of safety
  • Identify practical opportunities to simplify and improve HSE processes as the organisation continues to evolve
What You Bring
  • Strong HSE experience gained within renewable energy, infrastructure, construction, utilities or another project and asset focused environment
  • Experience working across construction projects, operational assets and contractor environments
  • Sound technical capability across HSE management systems, risk, incidents, audits and assurance
  • A practical approach with the ability to balance HSE requirements with commercial and operational priorities
  • Strong relationship building skills and the credibility to work effectively with contractors, project teams, operational leaders and senior stakeholders
  • The ability to influence outcomes and build safety ownership through engagement
  • Confidence working autonomously across multiple priorities and geographically dispersed stakeholders
  • A continuous improvement mindset and the ability to operate comfortably within a growing and evolving organisation
  • Relevant qualifications in Work Health and Safety, Environmental Management or a related discipline
Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is a broad HSE role offering exposure well beyond a single construction project or operational site.

You will work across the lifecycle of renewable energy assets, partnering with teams across development, construction, operations and asset management while gaining visibility across a growing national portfolio.

The business already has solid HSE foundations in place. The opportunity is to strengthen how these are applied in practice, improve contractor assurance and help leaders take greater ownership of safety as the organisation grows.

For someone looking to broaden their renewable energy experience, work with a diverse group of stakeholders and contribute to a business going through continued growth, this offers plenty of variety and scope.
